topics.title: The Box Model
topics.summary: Every element is a box made of content, padding, border and margin.
topics.description:
In CSS **every element is a rectangular box**. The box model describes the layers of that box from the inside out:

1. **Content** - the text, image or children.
2. **Padding** - space between the content and the border (inside the box, shows the background).
3. **Border** - the line around the padding.
4. **Margin** - transparent space outside the border that separates the element from its neighbours.

### Size calculation (default `content-box`)
`width` and `height` set only the **content** area. The visible size is:

```text
total width = width + padding-left + padding-right + border-left + border-right
```

For example, `width: 800px; padding: 50px; border: 20px solid;` gives a box that occupies **940px** horizontally (800 + 100 + 40). Margin is added on top of this for spacing, but it is not part of the box background.

### Block vs inline boxes
- **Block** boxes take the full available width and start on a new line, and respect all four margins/paddings and width/height.
- **Inline** boxes flow in a line; width/height are ignored and vertical margins have no effect.

### Inspecting the box
Open DevTools, pick an element and look at the **Box Model diagram** in the Computed tab: it shows the content, padding, border and margin values in different colors. This is the fastest way to debug unexpected spacing.

### Why it matters
Almost every layout bug ("why is it 20px too wide?", "why does it overflow?") comes from forgetting that padding and border are added to width. The next topic (`box-sizing`) fixes this.
keyPoints: Box = content + padding + border + margin
Default content-box: width/height are only the content
Padding shows the element background; margin is always transparent
Inline elements ignore width/height and vertical margins
Use DevTools box-model diagram to debug spacing
pitfalls: Adding padding to a width: 100% element and causing horizontal overflow
Expecting background color to fill the margin area
Applying width/height to a plain inline <span>

interview.a: Each element is a box with content, padding, border and margin layers. width/height apply to the content box by default; padding and border are added around it and margin sits outside.

interview.q: Do inline elements respect width and height?
interview.a: No. Width/height and vertical margins are ignored on non-replaced inline elements; use inline-block or block.

interview.q: Is margin part of the element's size?
interview.a: No. Margin is outside the border, is transparent and is not painted with the background, but it affects the space the element takes in layout.

topics.title: box-sizing and CSS Reset
topics.summary: border-box makes width include padding and border; a reset gives a predictable starting point.
topics.description:
`box-sizing` controls what `width` and `height` mean.

| Value | width applies to | 300px wide + 20px padding + 5px border |
|---|---|---|
| `content-box` (default) | content only | 350px on screen |
| `border-box` | content + padding + border | **300px** on screen |

`border-box` is far easier to reason about: the number you write is the size you get. That is why almost every project starts with:

```css
*,
*::before,
*::after {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}
```

### Inherit pattern (friendly to third-party widgets)
```css
html { box-sizing: border-box; }
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: inherit; }
```

### What is a CSS reset?
Browsers ship default styles (body margin 8px, h1 margins, list bullets). A **reset** removes or normalises them so you start from the same baseline in every browser.

- **Classic reset**: `* { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }` (used in the source course).
- **Normalize.css**: keeps useful defaults but fixes inconsistencies.
- **Modern reset**: small and opinionated, e.g. `img { max-width: 100%; display: block; }`, `body { line-height: 1.5; }`, form controls `font: inherit;`.

### Tips
- Do not reset `*` margin if you rely on default heading spacing - then your own spacing rules must replace them.
- A tiny reset is usually enough. Do not copy huge resets without understanding them.
keyPoints: content-box (default): width excludes padding/border
border-box: width includes padding and border - preferred
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box } is the standard rule
A reset normalises browser default styles
Keep resets small: margin, box-sizing, img, form font
pitfalls: Forgetting ::before and ::after in the universal selector
Using border-box and then being surprised that padding shrinks the content area
Copying a giant reset that removes focus outlines (hurts accessibility)

topics.title: Margin
topics.summary: Space outside an element: shorthand, auto centering, negative margins and margin collapsing.
topics.description:
**Margin** creates space *outside* the border. It pushes neighbouring elements away.

### Shorthand
| Values | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `margin: 10px` | all sides |
| `margin: 10px 20px` | top/bottom, left/right |
| `margin: 10px 20px 30px` | top, left/right, bottom |
| `margin: 10px 20px 30px 40px` | top, right, bottom, left (clockwise) |

Individual sides: `margin-top`, `margin-right`, `margin-bottom`, `margin-left`.

### margin: auto
On a block element with a set `width`, `margin: 0 auto;` centers it horizontally. Inside flex/grid, auto margins absorb free space (`margin-left: auto` pushes an item to the right).

### Negative margins
Allowed. They pull an element toward or over its neighbours - useful for overlaps and gutter tricks, but use sparingly.

### Margin collapsing
Vertical margins of **adjacent block siblings** collapse into the **larger one** (not the sum). A parent and its first/last child can collapse too if there is no padding, border or clearfix between them. Collapsing does **not** happen in flex or grid containers, with floats, absolutely positioned elements or `overflow` other than visible.

Ways to avoid surprises:
- use one-direction spacing (only `margin-bottom` or use `gap`),
- add `padding` or `border` to the parent,
- use `display: flow-root` on the parent.

### Logical margins
`margin-inline` and `margin-block` adapt to writing direction (see Logical Properties).
keyPoints: Margin is outside the border; always transparent
Shorthand order is clockwise: top, right, bottom, left
margin: 0 auto centers a block with a width
Adjacent vertical margins collapse to the larger value
gap in flex/grid is cleaner than margins between items
pitfalls: Child margin-top "leaking" out of the parent due to collapsing
margin: auto not centering because the element has no width
Horizontal auto margin does not vertically center a block in normal flow

topics.title: Padding
topics.summary: Space inside the border: shorthand, buttons and cards, and why negative padding does not exist.
topics.description:
**Padding** is the space between the content and the border, *inside* the element. The element's background and background image extend under the padding.

### Shorthand (same as margin)
- `padding: 10px;` all sides
- `padding: 5px 10px;` vertical | horizontal
- `padding: 1px 2px 2px;` top | horizontal | bottom
- `padding: 5px 1px 0 2px;` top | right | bottom | left

Individual: `padding-top`, `padding-right`, `padding-bottom`, `padding-left`.

### Differences from margin
| | padding | margin |
|---|---|---|
| Location | inside border | outside border |
| Background | painted | transparent |
| Negative values | **not allowed** | allowed |
| auto | not allowed | allowed |
| Collapses | never | vertical margins can |
| Clickable area | yes (part of element) | no |

### Typical uses
- Buttons: `padding: 12px 36px;` gives a comfortable click area.
- Cards and panels: `padding: 24px;` separates text from the edge.
- Making inline links bigger tap targets (`display: inline-block; padding: ...`).

### Percentages
Percentage padding is relative to the **width** of the containing block - even for top/bottom. This enables the classic aspect-ratio hack (`padding-top: 56.25%` for 16:9), now replaced by `aspect-ratio`.

### Tip
With `box-sizing: border-box` padding shrinks the content inside the declared width instead of growing the box.
keyPoints: Padding is inside the border and shows the background
Shorthand follows the same 1-2-3-4 value rules as margin
Negative padding is invalid
Percent padding is based on container width
Padding enlarges clickable/tappable area
pitfalls: Padding making a 100% wide box overflow when box-sizing is content-box
Using margin instead of padding for button size so only the text is clickable

topics.title: Borders, Radius and Outline
topics.summary: border shorthand, individual sides, border-radius shapes and the outline property.
topics.description:
### Border shorthand
`border: <width> <style> <color>;` for example `border: 2px solid #333;`.

Individual properties: `border-width`, `border-style`, `border-color`. Per side: `border-top`, `border-right`, `border-bottom`, `border-left` and even `border-top-width` etc.

**Styles**: `none`, `hidden`, `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `double`, `groove`, `ridge`, `inset`, `outset`. Without a style the border does not show!

Multiple values follow the usual clockwise rule: `border-style: dotted solid;` (top/bottom dotted, left/right solid).

### border-radius
Rounds the corners.

- `border-radius: 10px;` all corners
- `border-radius: 10px 20%;` top-left+bottom-right | top-right+bottom-left
- `border-radius: 15px 5px 10px 20px;` TL | TR | BR | BL
- `border-radius: 50%;` circle (on a square) or ellipse
- `border-radius: 999px;` pill shape
- Elliptical: `border-radius: 100% 0 / 100% 0;` horizontal / vertical radii

### Logical border shorthands
`border-inline` (left+right) and `border-block` (top+bottom) are newer shorthands: `border-block: 5px solid red;`.

### outline
`outline` draws a line **outside** the border, does not take space and does not follow border-radius in older browsers. Perfect for focus rings: `outline: 3px solid #2965f1; outline-offset: 2px;`.

### Other border tricks
- Triangles with zero-size box and transparent borders.
- `border-image` for gradient or image borders.
- Gradient borders: `border: 4px solid transparent; background: linear-gradient(...) border-box;`.
keyPoints: border: width style color - style is mandatory
border-radius: 50% makes circles; 999px makes pills
Each side and each property can be set independently
outline does not affect layout and is ideal for focus rings
border-inline / border-block are logical shorthands
pitfalls: Writing border: 2px red without a style (nothing renders)
Removing outline: none without a replacement focus style
Expecting border-radius to clip overflowing children (needs overflow: hidden)

topics.title: Overflow
topics.summary: Control what happens when content is bigger than its box: visible, hidden, scroll, auto and clip.
topics.description:
When content does not fit in its box it **overflows**. The `overflow` property decides what the browser does.

| Value | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `visible` | default; content spills outside the box |
| `hidden` | extra content is clipped, no scrollbars (but can still scroll programmatically) |
| `scroll` | scrollbars are always shown |
| `auto` | scrollbars only when needed - the usual choice |
| `clip` | like hidden but no scrolling at all and no new formatting context |

Control each axis: `overflow-x` and `overflow-y`. If one is not `visible`, the other cannot stay visible (it becomes `auto`).

### Common patterns
- **Scrollable panel**: fixed `height` / `max-height` + `overflow-y: auto`.
- **Horizontal scroller**: `overflow-x: auto; white-space: nowrap;` (as in the source demo).
- **Clipping children to rounded corners**: `border-radius` + `overflow: hidden`.
- **Clearing floats / containing margins**: `overflow: auto` or better `display: flow-root`.

### Text overflow
```css
.truncate {
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;   /* adds ... */
}
```
Multi-line clamp: `display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 3; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden;` (also standard `line-clamp` is arriving).

### Nice scrolling extras
- `scroll-behavior: smooth;`
- `overscroll-behavior: contain;` to stop scroll chaining
- `scrollbar-gutter: stable;` to avoid layout shift
- `scrollbar-width: thin;`
keyPoints: visible (default), hidden, scroll, auto, clip
auto shows scrollbars only when content overflows
overflow-x / overflow-y control axes separately
Ellipsis needs nowrap + overflow hidden + text-overflow
overflow other than visible creates a block formatting context
pitfalls: overflow: hidden cutting off box-shadows or dropdowns of children
position: sticky stops working inside an ancestor with overflow hidden/auto
Using scroll instead of auto and showing empty scrollbars on desktop

interview.q: Difference between overflow: auto and scroll?
interview.a: scroll always shows scrollbars; auto shows them only when content actually overflows.

interview.q: How do you create a single line text ellipsis?
interview.a: white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; and a constrained width.

interview.q: How to make a box scroll only horizontally?
interview.a: overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden; (usually with white-space: nowrap or a flex row).
